need: One generated machine-readable file listing capability -> requirement -> scenario -> test -> file -> symbol from in-code markers (Implements: docstrings, pytest req markers) and OpenSpec specs, in well under a second inside make.

searched.found: status --json already emits requirement->symbol and scenario->test edges; markers.implementers computes file:line and status drops it; no file is written. The edit hook exists but only lockstep init installs it.

searched.where: PyPI and GitHub release metadata for traceability tools
searched.query: requirements traceability from code markers, JSON graph export
searched.found: Nine candidates checked; none reads our marker syntax without adapters of the generator's size.

candidates.name: StrictDoc 0.32.1
candidates.covers: Requirements, source-file relation markers, JSON/HTML export.
candidates.misses: Requirements must live in its .sdoc files, not OpenSpec markdown.

candidates.name: Doorstop 3.2
candidates.misses: Links live in per-item YAML; no in-code markers.

candidates.name: sphinx-needs 9.3.0
candidates.covers: needs.json export, a known node shape.
candidates.misses: Needs a full Sphinx build; too slow for make.
candidates.reason: Node shape borrowed (id, type, title, links, version), runtime not adopted.

candidates.name: OpenFastTrace
candidates.covers: Covers: tags in code, tracing report.

candidates.name: LOBSTER (bmw-lobster-core 1.1.0)
candidates.covers: Python tags and pytest tests, JSON format.
candidates.misses: Different tag syntax; AGPL in a template others copy.
candidates.reason: Adapters cost as much as the generator; licence.

gap: No tool reads Implements: and req() markers with OpenSpec IDs; Lockstep's own parsers already do, so the file is a few dozen lines on top of status.
